title: Premier Doug Ford suggests 'ass whooping' for 2 boys connected to alleged assault of Hamilton cadet leader
summary: Ontario Premier Doug Ford commented on an alleged assault in Hamilton, saying the parents of two boys police say were involved should "give your kids a little ass whooping in the wood shed."

blocks.text: Hamilton·New
Ontario Premier Doug Ford commented on an alleged assault in Hamilton, saying the parents of two boys police say were involved should "give your kids a little ass whooping in the wood shed."
Police charged 12-year-old boy, 48-year-old woman with assault in Nov. 1 incident
Ford suggests ‘ass whooping’ for 2 boys connected to cadet assault
Ontario Premier Doug Ford says the parents of two boys allegedly involved in the assault of a Hamilton cadet leader should "give your kids a little ass whooping in the wood shed."

Ford's comments at a news conference come a week after the Hamilton Police Service said it charged a 12-year-old boy and a 48-year-old woman with assaulting a 59-year-old commanding officer for the Royal Canadian Air Cadets.

The cadet leader was supervising the distribution of Remembrance Day poppies at the Centre on Barton mall when two boys approached them and blew a loud air in the ears of young cadets he was with, police said in a release. The man followed the boys into a nearby restaurant to confront them and "a struggle ensued."

Police said a woman — who they later told CBC News is named Estela Quintanilla — jumped in to assist the boys and assaulted the cadet leader, causing him to fall. The 12-year-old hit him several times, police said.
The family of the cadet leader has identified him as Capt. Kenneth Kunkel. On Nov. 5, his daughter Kimberly Dietrich told CBC's Hanomansing Live that Kunkel was unable to walk.
Dietrich said her family was "taking it a day at a time," and her dad was "trying his hardest to recover."
Cadet leader faces life-altering injuries after ‘senseless’ attack | Hanomansing Live
The 12-year-old boy faces aggravated assault and assault level one charges, police said. The second boy was not arrested, police said, after officers were able to review footage of the incident.
The woman faces aggravated assault charges.
The charges have not been tested in court.

Ford has a history of commenting on criminal cases. Some lawyers have told CBC News that public officials should be careful about such comments, as they risk prejudicing juries and contributing to misinformation.

items: Ontario's premier has a habit of weighing in on criminal cases. Some lawyers say he should be more careful

blocks.text: "I just don't know how to process it," Dietrich said of the incident Thursday. "I don't know why someone would even think of doing something like that."
She said it's important to support veterans by wearing poppies.
Hamilton mayor-elect Keanin Loomis issued a statement about the incident Thursday, saying he is "deeply troubled" by it.
"My thoughts are with Kunkel, his family and the cadets during this difficult time. We wish him strength, healing and a full recovery," Loomis said.
